info.title: Clew connector protocol
info.summary: How a connector service and a Clew installation talk to each other.
info.description: A connector is an HTTP service of your own. It serves the routes tagged **Connector**; Clew loads its manifest and calls it as the acting person, with an RS256 assertion it can verify against the keys at the route tagged **Clew**. Shapes are the same JSON Schemas the instance validates with, published under `components.schemas` and, as one bundle, as `connector-protocol.schema.json` under `/api/protocol/`. Generate server stubs from this document or implement the paths by hand; the examples under `connectors/` in the repository are complete. Try `POST /api/protocol/manifest` with a manifest before any service exists.

retired.1: retired 2026-11-05: shared-secret (HS256) identity signing was replaced by RS256 installation keys (D44). Move the verifier to the installation's public keys and declare protocol 2.

tags.name: Connector
tags.description: Routes the connector serves and Clew calls. All JSON, all under the registered base URL. Every POST carries `Authorization: Bearer <assertion>` and `X-Clew-Connector-Key`; take the actor from the verified assertion, never from the body.
